1. The parts of the system (deployables, workers, Durable Objects, sandboxes/containers, clients/plugins) and how they connect, with the protocol or payload on each connection.
2. Where the agent loop runs, where the session state lives and how it is persisted and resumed.

4. Anything in its docs/notes that names trade-offs versus running pi-coding-agent locally.
Keep it to what the code and its docs show; mark anything inferred.

1	# tentacles
     2	
     3	tentacles runs coding-agent sessions remotely, on pi-durable, over infrastructure behind provider-neutral contracts, with Cloudflare as the first setup. A plugin for pi and Claude Code lets a local agent spawn, steer, question and collect those remote sessions the way it does local subagents.
     4	
     5	## Docs
     6	
     7	- **Docs**: `docs/`. Read its `README.md` before adding, editing, renaming or moving anything under it.
     8	- **Folders**: `technical-design/`, the shape of the system and how each part works; `product-design/`, what tentacles is and what it is like to use.
     9	- **Checks**: `pnpm check` · `pnpm test`

1 --- 2 title: "Runtime components" 3 summary: "The roles tentacles' shared logic reaches through provider-neutral contracts, what crosses between them, and how a provider plugs its implementation in." 4 created: "2026-11-09" 5 --- 6 7 # Runtime components 8 9 ## 🔭 Overview 10 11 tentacles runs as a set of roles: an API entry that is the only way in, a registry for everything that spans sessions, one session object per session running pi-durable, a workspace per session that holds the agent's files and runs its commands, model providers, a codemode sandbox, a managed browser for previews and a daily scheduler. tentacles' shared logic reaches each role through a contract, and a provider fills every contract, so another setup can replace the infrastructure without changing the plugin. No container holds a credential: the provider adds the tokens to requests outside the container. Cloudflare is the first provider; [deploy](providers/cloudflare/deploy.md) covers how it fills each role. 12 13 ## 🏗️ Architecture 14 15 ```mermaid 16 flowchart LR 17 subgraph dev["Developer machine"] 18 Plugin@{ shape: stadium, label: "tentacles plugin

token added outside the container"| GitHub 41 Browser -->|"preview URL"| Entry 42 Cron -->|"daily cleanup"| Registry 43 44 classDef grey fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#4b5563,color:#1f2937 45 classDef blue fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1f2937 46 classDef green fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937 47 classDef violet fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#1f2937 48 class Plugin grey 49 class Entry blue 50 class Registry,Session,Workspace,Models,Codemode,Browser,Cron green 51 class GitHub violet 52 ``` 53 54 The **API entry** checks the API key on every plugin request and socket, then routes it: listings and preview lookups go to the registry, and everything about one session goes to that session's object by its id. Its preview route turns a preview URL's token into a session and a port and hands the request to the session object. [worker-api](worker-api.md) lists its calls and the session socket. 55 56 The **registry** is the one store that spans sessions: an entry per session with its name, its parent, its status, the time its last run stopped, its settings and skill and agent names, and the session's preview while one is open. [sessions](sessions.md) lists the fields of each entry. 57 58 The **session object** is one live instance per session, keyed by its session id. It runs pi-durable's Harness over its own storage, with the question tool and the wake-up timer that resumes a run after an eviction. It creates the session's workspace at spawn and installs the tools the workspace returns, holds the parent's socket, sends each model call to the provider the settings name, and opens and closes the preview's browser. It never writes the status ahead of the run: it watches pi-durable's state and tells the registry each time the derived status changes. 59 60 The **workspace** holds the session's files under `/workspace` and runs the agent's commands on the cheapest backend that can run them, the isolate shell or the container. Its git reaches GitHub with the token added outside the container. [workspace](workspace.md) covers its contract, setup and tools. 61 62 The **model providers**, the **codemode sandbox**, the **browser** and the **scheduler** each answer one kind of call: a model call, a codemode script, opening or closing the preview's browser, and firing the daily cleanup job. 63 64 ## 🔌 Provider-neutral roles 65 66 Each component above plays a role that any provider has to fill. Several roles already sit behind an interface the pi libraries define: pi-durable takes its storage, its wake-up timer and its tools from the host, and pi-ai reaches models through providers. The plugin talks only to the Worker API and the session socket, so it does not change with the provider. 67 68 | Role | Contract | What the common logic asks it | Interface it builds on | 69 |---|---|---|---| 70 | Session host: one live instance per session, revived on demand | `SessionHost` | reach a session by id and run one of its operations: create, prompt, answer, close, messages, status, connect a socket, forward a preview request, delete | pi-durable's Harness opens over any host | 71 | Session storage | `SessionStorage` | pi-durable's storage for one session | pi-durable's storage adapter | 72 | Wake-up timer | `WakeTimer` | set or clear the one timer that resumes a run after an eviction | pi-durable's `onWake`; the host writes the timer | 73 | Parent socket | `ParentChannel` | send the session state to every socket the parent holds open | none | 74 | Registry of sessions and their preview | `RegistryStore` | add an entry, record a status and the time a run stops, list one parent's sessions, open a preview and return its token, resolve and clear a preview, remove an entry, find the sessions stopped before a given time | none | 75 | Workspace: the session's files and the backends that run its commands | `Workspace` | `create(init)`: set up the workspace at spawn from the repository URL or none, the git identity, the container's size and image, and the skills and context archives, and return the tools the harness installs, each with its replay policy and its own execute; `forward`: hand a preview request to a port and return the app's answer, 502 when nothing listens | pi-durable's tool registrations | 76 | Browser | `Browser` | open a browser for the session's preview, returning the CDP URL agent-browser connects to, and close it | agent-browser speaks CDP to any URL | 77 | Preview routing | `PreviewRouter` | the public URL a preview token is served on | none | 78 | Models | `ModelProviders` | every model provider the session's settings can name | pi-ai providers | 79 | Daily cleanup | `Scheduler` | run a job once a day | none | 80 | Codemode sandbox | `CodeSandbox` | the sandbox codemode scripts run in | pi-durable's codemode sandbox | 81 | API entry: auth and routing | none, the Worker API itself | nothing: the API entry runs the API handlers | [worker-api](worker-api.md) | 82 83 A provider implements every contract in the table. The common logic (the API handlers, the session logic with its lifecycle and deletion, the preview handler, the cleanup job and the remote agent's tools other than the workspace's) and the pi libraries are the same for every provider. A deploy uses one provider for every role, and a variable read by the deploy picks the provider. 1 --- 2 title: "Sessions" 3 summary: "What tentacles stores about a remote session, how a session runs from spawn to deletion, the skills, agents and context files it carries, and the daily job that deletes sessions a month after their last run." 4 created: "2026-11-09" 5 --- 6 7 # Sessions 8 9 ## 🔭 Overview 10 11 A session is one remote agent: a session object keyed by its session id, where pi-durable keeps its conversations and tentacles keeps a record of who started it, with which settings, and in what state it is. The registry keeps one entry per session so the list call returns a parent's sessions with their status in one call. At spawn, a session sets up its workspace and then starts running; a failed setup leaves it failed instead. It goes idle or failed when a run stops, waits while its agent asks a question, and stays readable after it is closed. A session also carries the skills and agent definitions its parent sent at spawn, which its agent finds by name, and the context files, which sit in `/workspace/context`. A daily job deletes every session whose last run stopped more than a month ago. 12 13 ## 🗺️ A session from spawn to deletion 14 15 ```mermaid 16 sequenceDiagram 17 autonumber 18 actor P as Parent agent 19 participant H as Plugin 20 participant W as Worker 21 participant R as Registry 22 participant S as Session 23 participant Ws as Workspace 24 participant M as Model 25 P->>H: spawn with name, prompt, settings, skill, agent and context paths 26 H->>H: check the files, pack the archives 27 H->>W: create 28 W->>S: create 29 S->>S: store the record and the documents 30 S->>R: add the entry with settings, skill and agent names 31 S->>Ws: create: clone the repository, expand the skills and context 32 Ws-->>S: the workspace's tools, or the setup error 33 S-->>P: session id once the first run starts, or the setup error 34 loop every run 35 S->>S: expand the prompt's named skills 36 S->>M: model call 37 M-->>S: text and tool calls 38 S->>Ws: tool call 39 Ws-->>S: tool result 40 opt the agent asks the parent 41 S->>R: status waiting 42 S-->>H: state with the question 43 H-->>P: wake with the question 44 P->>W: answer 45 W->>S: answer, the run continues 46 end 47 end 48 S->>R: status idle or failed, time the run stopped 49 S-->>H: state with the last entry 50 H-->>P: wake with the result 51 P->>W: prompt for a new run, or close 52 W->>S: prompt or close 53 Note over W,S: a month after the last run stopped,
the daily job deletes the session and drops its entry 54 ``` 55 56 The parent spawns with a name, a first prompt, its settings and any skill, agent and context paths (1). The plugin checks the files and packs them into up to three archives (2), and sends create through the Worker to a new session (3, 4). The session stores its record and its skills, agents and context documents (5) and adds its registry entry (6). It then creates its workspace, which clones the repository and expands the skills and context archives into `/workspace` (7), and hands back the workspace's tools or the setup error (8). The session answers with its id once the first run has started, or with the setup error, which leaves it failed (9; [workspace](workspace.md)). 57 58 In every run, the session expands any skill the prompt names (10), sends the conversation to the model (11, 12) and runs the tools the model calls in the workspace (13, 14). When the agent asks the parent, the session waits, the plugin wakes the parent with the question and the answer continues the run (15 to 19; [question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md)). 59 60 When a run ends, the session records the new status and the time the run stopped in the registry (20), and sends the state with the run's last entry, which the plugin turns into a wake (21, 22). A prompt starts a new run and close stops the session (23, 24; [worker-api](worker-api.md)). A month after the last run stopped, the daily job deletes the session (see Daily cleanup below). 61 62 ## 💽 Modeling 63 64 ```mermaid 65 erDiagram 66 REGISTRY_ENTRY ||--|| SESSION : "points to" 67 SESSION ||--o{ CONVERSATION : "has (pi-durable)" 68 SESSION ||--o{ QUESTION : "asked (one document)" 69 SESSION ||--o| SKILLS_DOCUMENT : "holds" 70 SESSION ||--o| AGENTS_DOCUMENT : "holds" 71 SESSION ||--o| CONTEXT_DOCUMENT : "holds" 72 SKILLS_DOCUMENT ||--o{ SKILL : "lists" 73 AGENTS_DOCUMENT ||--o{ AGENT : "lists" 74 REGISTRY_ENTRY { 75 string session_id PK 76 string name 77 string parent_harness 78 string parent_session_id 79 string status "nullable" 80 datetime last_stopped "nullable" 81 int preview_port "nullable" 82 string preview_token "nullable" 83 json settings "written at create" 84 json skill_names "written at create" 85 json agent_names "written at create" 86 } 87 SESSION { 88 string id PK 89 string name 90 string parent_harness 91 string parent_session_id 92 json settings 93 boolean closed 94 datetime last_stopped "nullable" 95 text setup_error "nullable" 96 } 97 QUESTION { 98 string id PK 99 text text 100 text answer "nullable" 101 } 102 SKILLS_DOCUMENT { 103 json skills "written once at spawn" 104 } 105 AGENTS_DOCUMENT { 106 json agents "written once at spawn" 107 } 108 CONTEXT_DOCUMENT { 109 boolean sent "written once at spawn" 110 } 111 SKILL { 112 string name 113 string description 114 string path "/workspace/skills/name/SKILL.md" 115 } 116 AGENT { 117 string name 118 string description 119 text prompt 120 } 121 ``` 122 123 pi-durable's conversations (the root, its forks and subagent conversations) live inside the session object as pi-durable stores them. tentacles adds the other entities. 124 125 ### 🧠 Session 126 127 SESSION is the record each session object keeps next to pi-durable's history. `id` is the session id the object is keyed by. `name` is required and given by the parent at spawn; it is what the parent's status line shows. `parent_harness` (pi or claude) and `parent_session_id` identify the parent: its harness and that harness's session id. `settings` holds what the parent chose at spawn, with the plugin's defaults for anything the parent left out: provider, model, effort level, image and size, and optionally the repository tentacles clones into the workspace. close sets `closed`, and a prompt that reopens the session clears it. `last_stopped` is the time the session's last run stopped, and is empty while the first run is going. `setup_error` holds why the workspace's setup failed at spawn, and is empty for every session whose setup succeeded (see [workspace](workspace.md)). 128 129 The session state it sends the parent also carries its settings and the names of its skills and agents. 130 131 The session's status is not a field. The session object watches pi-durable's state and derives it: a run going is running, an unanswered question is waiting, no run with `closed` set is closed, no run with the last run's failure recorded is failed (pi-durable keeps why the run failed), and no run otherwise is idle. A `setup_error` makes the status failed, with that error as the failure's detail. Each time the derived status changes, the session reports it to the registry and sends the session state to the parent, so a status always follows something the session did. 132 133 > [!NOTE] Why the session records a failed setup itself 134 > pi-durable records a failure only when a run ends, and the setup fails before any run exists. The session keeps the setup error in its own record, which makes a failed setup the one status that does not come from pi-durable. It happens only before the first run, since the first run starts only after a successful setup. 135 136 ### 📒 Registry entry 137 138 REGISTRY_ENTRY lives in the registry, one for the whole deploy, with one entry per session: the session id, its name, the parent's harness and session id, the session's status (the same values as the session's derived status, closed included, and empty until the session reports its first one) and `last_stopped`, the time the last run stopped. When the session adds its entry at create, it also writes three values that never change: `settings`, and `skill_names` and `agent_names`, the names of the skills and agent definitions its spawn sent, which it reads from the archives. The registry records `last_stopped` itself when a status change reports a stopped run, keeps it when one stopped status follows another, and clears it when a new run starts. The session updates its entry on every state change, so the list call and the plugin's start-up sync get each session's status without asking each session. The daily cleanup job picks its candidates from the registry's `last_stopped`, and drops the entry after it deletes the session. 139 140 `preview_port` and `preview_token` hold the session's preview while one is open, and are empty otherwise. A session has at most one preview, and only to validate the app in the preview's browser; the agent validates anything else, such as an API, inside the workspace with no preview. `preview_port` is the workspace port the preview exposes. `preview_token` is a random UUID that the registry generates when the preview tool opens a preview. It is the only value the registry returns for the new preview, so a preview URL carries neither the API key nor the session id. Opening a preview while one is open replaces it: the previous token stops working and its browser closes. When the run stops, the registry clears both fields. [workspace](workspace.md) covers how the agent opens and uses a preview. 141 142 > [!TIP] Rejected: listing the session objects directly 143 > The session host reaches a session only by its id, and session objects cannot be enumerated or queried across instances, so "the sessions of this parent" has no answer without a store that spans sessions. The registry is that store, and holding the status there spares the plugin one status call per session. 144 145 ### ❓ Question 146 147 QUESTION is a question the session's agent asked with `ask_parent`: its id, its text and its answer, empty until the parent answers. Every question of the session lives in one session-wide document, one entry per question, and an entry stays after its answer. The id is the id of the asking tool call. When an eviction makes the tool run again, the replay finds its question in the document and keeps the id. If the answer already arrived, the replay returns the answer without asking again. The waiting question is the one with no answer whose tool call is still live; an aborted or finished call takes its question out of waiting. [question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md) follows the question to the parent and back. 148 149 ### 📚 Skills and agents documents 150 151 A skill is a folder that holds a SKILL.md and whatever the skill points to. An agent definition is a file whose frontmatter names a subagent and whose body is that subagent's prompt. The skills document and the agents document are pi-durable documents of the session, written once at spawn. A skill entry holds the skill's name and description, which the prompt lists. It also holds the full path of its SKILL.md in the workspace, which the skill tool and a prompt expansion point the agent to. An agent entry holds the agent's name, description and prompt, which the subagent tool starts a subagent with. Agent definitions live only here and never enter the workspace. 152 153 The session keeps no archive. It reads every archive at create to build the documents and hands the skills and context archives to the workspace's create, which expands them into `/workspace/skills` and `/workspace/context` once, at spawn. The agents archive goes no further, since agent definitions never enter the workspace. Deleting the session clears the documents, the workspace and the rest of its storage. 154 155 CONTEXT_DOCUMENT records whether the spawn sent context files, so the prompt section renders without reading the workspace. The session state, the list and the registry entry carry nothing about the context. 156 157 The API key and the Claude and GitHub credentials are Worker secrets, and none of these entities stores them. 158 159 ## 🟢 Lifecycle 160 161 ```mermaid 162 stateDiagram-v2 163 [*] --> Running : spawn, setup succeeds (first prompt) 164 [*] --> Failed : spawn, setup fails 165 Running --> Idle : run finishes 166 Running --> Waiting : ask_parent asks 167 Waiting --> Running : answer 168 Running --> Failed : run fails 169 Idle --> Running : prompt 170 Failed --> Running : prompt 171 Closed --> Running : prompt (reopens) 172 Running --> Closed : close (aborts) 173 Waiting --> Closed : close (aborts) 174 Idle --> Closed : close 175 Failed --> Closed : close 176 Idle --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped 177 Failed --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped 178 Closed --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped 179 Deleted --> [*] 180 181 note right of Running : working, prompts follow up or steer 182 note right of Waiting : question shown to the parent,
prompts queue as steers until answered 183 note right of Failed : like idle, shows the last run failed,
or why the setup failed 184 note left of Closed : kept and readable, a prompt reopens it 185 186 classDef working fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e293b 187 classDef waiting fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#1e293b 188 classDef done fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1e293b 189 classDef failed fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#1e293b 190 classDef ended fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#64748b,color:#1e293b 191 class Running working 192 class Waiting waiting 193 class Idle done 194 class Failed failed 195 class Closed,Deleted ended 196 ``` 197 198 A session starts running when the parent spawns it, since spawn carries the first prompt; the session stores the skills and agent definitions and sets up its workspace before the run starts. When the setup fails, the session starts failed: its first run never starts, it has no workspace to use, and the failure carries the setup error. While it runs, a prompt from the parent follows up or steers. An eviction is not a state: pi-durable resumes the run by the session's alarm and the session stays running. 199 200 When the agent asks a question, the session waits. The conversation cannot continue until the parent answers. A prompt sent meanwhile is a steer whatever its mode, and reaches the agent after the answer; it neither answers nor cancels the question. 201 202 A run ends in one of two ways. When it finishes, the session is idle. When the run fails on an error it cannot recover from, the session is failed: it behaves like idle and records why the last run failed. The plugin notifies the parent either way, and a prompt on either starts a new run. The session's preview, if one is open, closes when a run stops. 203 204 close aborts whatever the session is doing and leaves it closed: kept in its session object, where its history and state stay readable until it is deleted. close sets `closed` and aborts any run; the status turns closed once the session sees no run and `closed` set, at once for an idle or failed session. A prompt on a closed session clears `closed` and starts a new run, whether sent as a follow-up or a steer, and the status leaves closed once the run starts. 205 206 The month before deletion counts from when the last run stops: when it finishes, fails or is aborted by close. Closing a session that is already idle or failed aborts no run, so its month keeps counting from when its last run stopped. A session is never deleted while a run is going, including while a question waits inside it, and reading a session (its messages, its status, a socket connecting) does not renew the month. 207 208 ## 🧩 Skills and agents 209 210 ### 🏗️ Which conversations get them 211 212 ```mermaid 213 flowchart LR 214 subgraph root["Root conversation"] 215 R1@{ shape: rect, label: "Workspace tools,
codemode, preview" } 216 R2@{ shape: rect, label: "Skills extension
document, section, skill tool" } 217 R3@{ shape: rect, label: "Agents extension

question tool, tentacles instructions" } 219 end 220 subgraph child["Child"] 221 C1@{ shape: rect, label: "Workspace tools,

codemode, preview" } 227 G2@{ shape: rect, label: "Skills extension" } 228 end 229 root -->|"spawns, keeps all but the root extension"| child 230 child -->|"spawns, also drops the agents extension"| grand 231 classDef green fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937 232 classDef amber fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#1f2937 233 class R1,C1,G1 green 234 class R2,R3,R4,C2,C3,G2 amber 235 ``` 236 237 Skills and agents are each one pi-durable extension that owns its document, its prompt section and its tool. Every conversation in a session gets the skills extension: the root, its children and their children. The root and its children also get the agents extension, so a child can spawn subagents of its own; a grandchild cannot. Only the root carries the question tool and tentacles' own instructions. An extension leaves its section out of the prompt when the section has nothing to list. 238 239 > [!NOTE] Why skills and agents are extensions of their own 240 > Only the skill tool, the subagent tool and their sections read the skills and agents, and they never change after spawn, while the session record gets a new revision at every run end. A document owned by each extension keeps them out of the record's revisions and lets either extension be taken out without touching the record. 241 242 ### 🚀 What a spawn sends 243 244 The parent passes skill folder paths, agent definition paths and context paths to the spawn tool, on pi and on Claude Code alike. The plugin's helper stats every path, reads only each skill's SKILL.md and each agent definition file, checks them, and packs up to three archives, each a gzip-compressed tar file of at most 5 MB: 245 246 - The skills archive holds one folder per skill at its top level: `/SKILL.md` and everything beside it. 247 - The agents archive holds one agent definition file per agent at its top level, named `.md` after the agent. 248 - The context archive holds one entry per context path at its top level (see Context files). 249 250 The helper's packer reads the files while it packs. It follows symlinks and packs what each one points to, writes an entry for every folder, and keeps each file's permission bits, so a skill's executable scripts stay executable in `/workspace/skills`. A skill's SKILL.md goes into the archive as the helper read it, with its frontmatter repaired, in place of the file on disk. The helper checks each archive's size once the archive is packed. 251 252 Each archive is optional, and a spawn sends any of them without the others. The create call carries them next to the name, the parent, the settings and the first prompt (see [worker-api](worker-api.md)). 253 254 ```mermaid 255 flowchart TD 256 A["Paths from the spawn call"] --> SP & AP & CP 257 subgraph skills["Skills, each folder on its own"] 258 SP{"path exists and holds SKILL.md?"} -->|Yes| SF{"frontmatter: name matches folder and follows the rules, description 1-1024?"} 259 SF -->|Yes| SU{"name unique among the skills?"} 260 SU -->|Yes| SZ{"packed skills archive within 5 MB?"} 261 end 262 subgraph agents["Agents, each file on its own"] 263 AP{"path exists and holds a file?"} -->|Yes| AF{"frontmatter: name matches file name and follows the rules, description 1-1024, body not empty?"} 264 AF -->|Yes| AU{"name unique among the agents?"} 265 AU -->|Yes| AZ{"packed agents archive within 5 MB?"} 266 end 267 subgraph context["Context, each path on its own"] 268 CP{"path exists and is a file or a folder?"} -->|Yes| CU{"basename unique among the context paths?"} 269 CU -->|Yes| CZ{"packed context archive within 5 MB?"} 270 end 271 SP & SF & SU & SZ -->|No| SE["Skills problem, with its path"] 272 AP & AF & AU & AZ -->|No| AE["Agents problem, with its path"] 273 CP & CU & CZ -->|No| CE["Context problem, with its path"] 274 SZ -->|Yes| J{"any problem collected?"} 275 AZ -->|Yes| J 276 CZ -->|Yes| J 277 SE --> J 278 AE --> J 279 CE --> J 280 J -->|Yes| N(("Spawn error: every problem, in Skills, Agents and Context groups")) 281 J -->|No| O(("Spawn proceeds")) 282 classDef green fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937 283 classDef blue fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1f2937 284 classDef red fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#1f2937 285 class A,O green 286 class SP,SF,SU,SZ,AP,AF,AU,AZ,CP,CU,CZ,J blue 287 class SE,AE,CE,N red 288 ``` 289 290 The helper checks each kind apart, every path on its own, and keeps going after a problem so it reports them all. A skill follows the Agent Skills specification. Its name is 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, with no leading, trailing or doubled hyphen, and equals its folder's name. Its description is 1 to 1024 characters. An agent definition is a file whose frontmatter name and description follow the same rules as a skill's, whose name equals the file's name without `.md`, and whose body is not empty. Names are unique within each group, and each packed archive stays within 5 MB; a kind with a problem is not packed, so its size is not checked. When anything fails, the spawn tool returns every problem with its path, in a Skills, an Agents and a Context group, and nothing reaches tentacles. 291 292 Frontmatter is read as YAML. A top-level value on one line that YAML rejects as written, such as a description holding `: `, is read as a quoted string. The helper then packs the file with that value quoted, so the session reads valid frontmatter. Frontmatter that is still not valid YAML is a problem with its path. 293 294 > [!NOTE] Why a rejected value is read as a quoted string 295 > Definitions written for other assistants often carry such values, and those assistants accept them. Reading them as quoted strings keeps those definitions usable without editing them. 296 297 The session takes these values from an agent definition: 298 299 | From the file | Becomes | 300 |---|---| 301 | frontmatter `name` | the agent's name, verbatim | 302 | frontmatter `description` | the agent's description, verbatim | 303 | the body | the agent's prompt, verbatim, without the frontmatter | 304 | any other frontmatter field, such as tools, model, skills, color or permissionMode | nothing | 305 306 Every subagent gets the session's model and the tools of its level in the session, whatever its definition declares. 307 308 ### 📩 How the archives move 309 310 #### 🧳 At spawn 311 312 ```mermaid 313 sequenceDiagram 314 autonumber 315 actor P as Parent agent 316 participant H as Plugin helper 317 participant W as Worker 318 participant S as Session 319 participant DB as Session storage 320 participant R as Registry 321 participant Ws as Workspace 322 P->>+H: spawn with skill, agent and context paths 323 H->>H: stat every path, read and check each SKILL.md and agent file 324 alt a check fails 325 H-->>P: every problem with its path, grouped by kind 326 else every check passes 327 H->>H: pack one archive per kind that has paths 328 H->>+W: create with the archives 329 W->>+S: create 330 S->>DB: skills, agents and context documents 331 S->>R: add the entry with settings, skill and agent names 332 S->>Ws: create with the skills and context archives 333 alt the setup succeeds 334 Ws-->>S: the workspace's tools 335 S->>S: start the first run 336 S-->>W: started 337 W-->>H: session id 338 H-->>P: session id 339 else the setup fails 340 Ws-->>S: the setup error 341 S->>R: status failed 342 S-->>-W: the setup error 343 W-->>-H: the setup error 344 H-->>-P: the setup error 345 end 346 end 347 ``` 348 349 The parent calls the spawn tool with paths (1). The plugin's helper stats every path and reads and checks each SKILL.md and agent definition file (2). On any failure, the helper returns every problem as the spawn tool's result and sends nothing (3). Otherwise it packs one archive for each kind that has paths (4) and sends create with them (5), which the Worker hands to the session (6). The session reads every archive again to build the skills and agents documents and writes the context document (7). When it cannot read one or more archives, create returns one error that names each invalid archive and its problem, and the session stores nothing (see [worker-api](worker-api.md)). It adds its registry entry with the settings and the skill and agent names it read (8), and creates its workspace with the skills and context archives (9), which the provider expands into `/workspace/skills`, one folder per skill, and `/workspace/context`. When the setup succeeds, the workspace hands back its tools (10), the session starts the first run (11), and create answers with the session id once the run has started (12 to 14). When the setup fails, the workspace hands back the setup error (15), the session records it and reports the failed status (16), and create answers with the error (17 to 19). 350 351 > [!NOTE] Why the archives travel in create 352 > Only the workspace's setup reads the skills and context archives, and it runs once, at spawn. Handing the archives to create lets the session drop them once the files are in `/workspace`, so the session never stores them twice. 353 354 #### 💬 In a prompt that names a skill 355 356 ```mermaid 357 sequenceDiagram 358 autonumber 359 actor P as Parent 360 participant S as Session 361 participant D as Skills document 362 participant A as Conversation 363 P->>S: create or prompt 364 S->>S: find /skill:name and /name triggers 365 alt a trigger names a skill the session holds 366 S->>D: the skill's SKILL.md path 367 D-->>S: path 368 S->>A: prompt with each trigger replaced by a pointer block 369 else no trigger names a held skill 370 S->>A: prompt as written 371 end 372 ``` 373 374 The session expands every prompt, the first one included, before the conversation admits it (1, 2). `/skill:` and `/` name a skill when the word after the slash is one of the session's skill names and the trigger stands on its own, with whitespace or the start or end of the text on each side. For each one, the session takes the skill's path from the skills document (3, 4) and replaces the `/skill:` or `/` in place with a block that points at the skill (5); a skill named twice gets a block at each one. A prompt with no such name reaches the conversation as written (6), and so does any `/word` that names no skill, sits inside a path or has punctuation attached. The conversation keeps the expanded prompt, so the session's messages show what the agent saw. 375 376 The prompt "Run /implement on the api repo" reaches the agent as: 377 378 ```text 379 Run 380 Read /workspace/skills/implement/SKILL.md before acting on this skill. Paths it names, such as references/ or scripts/, are relative to /workspace/skills/implement/. 381 on the api repo 382 ``` 383 384 > [!NOTE] Why the block points at the skill instead of holding it 385 > The agent reads SKILL.md with its read tool when it acts on the bl

     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	The Worker's API is the plugin's only way to reach tentacles: seven calls (create, prompt, answer, close, messages, status, list) and one socket per session. Every request and every socket carries the API key, and the plugin reads the Worker's URL and the key from environment variables. The socket sends one construct, the session state, when it connects and again on every change, and the status call returns the same construct. Calls on an existing session succeed, closed ones included; a deleted or unknown session returns an error.
    12	
    13	## ♠️ What it exposes
    14	
    15	| Member | Takes | Answers | Who asks |
    16	|---|---|---|---|
    17	| `create` | the name, the parent, the settings, the first prompt, and optionally a skills archive, an agents archive and a context archive (see below) | starts the session, stores its skills and agent definitions, sets up its workspace from the repository and the skills and context archives, waits until its first run has started and returns its session id; when the setup fails, returns an error naming the cause and leaves the session failed | the spawn tool |
    18	| `prompt` | the session id, the text, and a mode: follow-up or steer | sends the text to the session; on an idle, failed or closed session it starts a new run, reopening a closed one; a prompt sent while a question waits is a steer whatever its mode, and queues until the answer | the prompt tool |
    19	| `answer` | the session id, the question id and the answer text | resolves the waiting question, and the run continues | the answer tool |
    20	| `close` | the session id | aborts whatever the session is doing and closes it | the close tool |
    21	| `messages` | the session id and a count, 1 when absent | the last entries of the root conversation, as many as the count | the messages tool |
    22	| `status` | the session id | the session state at any time | the plugin, when it needs one session's state |
    23	| `list` | the parent | all of the parent's sessions from the registry, closed ones included, each with its id, name, status, settings and the names of its skills and agents | the list tool and the start-up sync |
    24	| socket | the session id, on connect | the session state on connect and on every change | the helper's watch, one socket per session |
    25	
    26	A message is any entry in the root conversation's history: a user prompt, the agent's text, a tool call or its result, a subagent's result. The last N messages are the last N entries, returned unshortened; the calling agent handles their length. `messages` does not read subagent conversations.
    27	
    28	The registry entry carries each session's name, status, settings and skill and agent names, so `list` answers without a call per session.
    29	
    30	A call or a socket on a deleted or unknown session, or an answer to a question that is not waiting, returns an error with a message. The plugin hands that message to the parent agent as a tool failure.
    31	
    32	## 🚀 What create takes
    33	
    34	| Input | What it holds |
    35	|---|---|
    36	| name | required; the status line shows the session by it |
    37	| parent | the parent's harness (pi or claude) and that harness's session id |
    38	| settings | provider, model, effort, image and size, and optionally a repository: its `https://` (or `http://`) URL and a shallow-or-full clone flag |
    39	| prompt | the first prompt; the run starts on it |
    40	| skills | optional; a gzip-compressed tar file of at most 5 MB with one skill folder per top-level entry |
    41	| agents | optional; a gzip-compressed tar file of at most 5 MB with one agent definition file per top-level entry |
    42	| context | optional; a gzip-compressed tar file of at most 5 MB with one top-level entry per file or folder the parent sent |
    43	
    44	Create's body is JSON and carries each archive base64-encoded, which makes it a third larger than the file. Three archives at the 5 MB limit come to about 20 MB.
    45	
    46	The plugin fills every unset setting from its defaults, so create always carries provider, model, effort, image and size. A repository is optional; the workspace's setup clones it into `/workspace/repo` (see [workspace](workspace.md)). Its URL is an `https://` (or `http://`) URL, since the workspace adds the GitHub token to HTTPS requests only, and a create with any other form, such as a bare `github.com/owner/name` or `git@github.com:owner/name`, fails the schema check.
    47	
    48	The plugin's helper checks the skills, agent definitions and context paths on the parent's machine and packs the archives only when every check passes, so the problems it finds reach the parent as the spawn tool's result and no create call is sent. [sessions](sessions.md) covers the checks, in its Skills and agents and Context files sections, and what the session does with each archive.
    49	
    50	The session reads each archive again and runs the same checks, reading frontmatter the same way the helper does. When it cannot read one or more archives, create returns one error that names each invalid archive and its problem. That happens when the file is not a gzip-compressed tar, a file in the skills archive sits outside a skill folder, a skill folder has no SKILL.md, a file in the agents archive is not at its top level, or a skill or agent definition breaks a rule. The session then stores nothing and starts no run. It hands the skills archive to the workspace as sent. The context archive is checked only for being readable, and an empty one is accepted; the session hands it to the workspace as sent. A create that does not come through the helper therefore puts every definition in `/workspace/skills` as written, including one the helper would have quoted.
    51	
    52	Once the archives pass, create sets up the session's workspace and answers only when the setup ends. When the setup fails, create returns an error whose message names the cause in plain words: a repository URL that does not exist, a token that cannot read the repository, GitHub not answering, or an archive that cannot be expanded; any other error comes back as it was captured. The session stays, failed, with that error as its failure, and no run starts (see [sessions](sessions.md)).
    53	
    54	## 📡 Session state
    55	
    56	The session state carries the session's status (running, waiting, idle, failed or closed), its settings, the names of its skills and agents, the question while one waits, and the failure when the last run failed or the workspace's setup failed. The question holds its id and its text (see [question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md)). When a run just finished, the state also carries the run's last entry, so the finish wake needs no messages call. A session already idle when the socket connects sends its state without the last entry, and the helper fetches it with `messages`. The socket sends the state when it connects and again on every change; status returns it too. [sessions](sessions.md) lists the states and the events that move a session between them.
    57	
    58	> [!NOTE] Why the session state is one construct
    59	> The finish notice, a new question, the status line, a reconnecting parent and the status call all read the same state, so each of them sees the same session, and a parent that was not connected when something changed learns it from the state sent on connect.
    60

     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	tentacles lets an agent on pi or Claude Code start coding agents that run remotely, on Cloudflare, and work with them the way it works with local subagents: spawn them, prompt and steer them, see when they stop, answer their questions and close them. The parent agent does all of it through a set of tools; nothing of a remote agent runs on the developer's machine. When the parent goes away, a remote agent keeps working and waits on its questions, and the parent finds it when it comes back. Its work stays in its workspace for as long as the remote agent exists: what it pushes survives the remote agent's deletion, and what it does not push goes with the remote agent a month after its last run. Every commit a remote agent makes is authored by the name and email the deploy sets, whoever spawned the agent.
    12	
    13	## 🚀 Spawning a remote agent
    14	
    15	The parent spawns a remote agent with a name, a first prompt and its settings: the provider, the model, the effort level, the container image and size, and optionally a repository to work on. The name is required; the status line and the list show the remote agent by its name. Any setting the parent leaves out takes the plugin's default, which the person can change through environment variables. Spawn answers once the remote agent's workspace is set up, with the repository cloned and its skills and context in place, and the agent then starts working on the first prompt. When the setup fails, spawn returns the reason, such as a repository URL that does not exist or a token that cannot read the repository, and spawn leaves the remote agent failed with that reason; it never starts working.
    16	
    17	With a repository in its settings, the remote agent starts with it cloned. Without one, it clones whatever its prompt names. Claude models run on the person's own Claude subscription, and models from other providers are available too.
    18	
    19	[workspace](../technical-design/workspace.md) covers the workspace's setup, its tools and what survives a container stop.
    20

    22	
    23	The parent can also send context files, the files and folders on its machine that the repository does not hold, such as a change's scratch files, by passing their paths at spawn. The remote agent finds each one in `/workspace/context` under its own name, outside the repository. The copy is fixed at spawn: the remote agent can change it, but its changes stay in its workspace and never come back to the parent, so work that needs different files goes to a new remote agent. The remote agent is told only that the parent sent files and that they are in `/workspace/context`, so the parent says in its handoff what the files are and how to use them. [sessions](../technical-design/sessions.md) covers how the context reaches the remote agent.
    24	
    25	## 💬 Prompting and steering
    26	
    27	While a remote agent works, the parent can send it a prompt as a follow-up, which the agent takes up after its current turn, or as a steer, which redirects it mid-run. A prompt to an agent that has finished starts it working again.
    28	
    29	Nobody watches a remote agent live. The parent reads what it did through the messages tool: its last message by default, or the last N, where a message is any entry of its conversation (prompts, its text, tool calls and results, subagent results).     30	
    31	A prompt can name one of the remote agent's skills, as `/skill:<name>` or `/<name>` standing on its own, with a space or the start or end of the prompt on each side. A name the remote agent does not hold, or one inside a path or with punctuation attached, stays as written.
    32	
    33	## 📊 The status line
    34	
    35	The harness shows a status line with the name and status of each open remote agent: running, waiting on a question, idle or failed. The status line hides closed ones, but the list tool still returns them.
    36	
    37	The list belongs to the parent's harness session. When the harness reopens that session, the plugin refreshes the list from tentacles, so the status line shows each agent's current status, including changes made while the parent was away. A forked parent starts with no remote agents of its own.
    38	
    39	The list also returns each remote agent's settings and the names of its skills and agents, so a parent that comes back later knows what each remote agent can do.
    40	
    41	## ⏰ Finish and failure wakes
    42	
    43	When a remote agent's run finishes, the plugin wakes the parent with that agent's last message, so the parent can read the result without another call. When a run fails on an error the agent cannot recover from, the plugin wakes the parent with the failure. In both cases the remote agent stays available: a prompt starts it on a new run.
    44	
    45	> [!WARNING] A headless parent is never woken
    46	> A parent running headless (`claude -p`) gets no wake, as with local subagents. It learns that a remote agent finished or asked something only by calling the tools.
    47	
    48	## 🧩 Skills and agents inside a remote agent
    49	
    50	A remote agent sees its skills and agent definitions by name and description, and loads a skill when a task matches it, reading its instructions and the files they point to. It installs whatever a skill needs to run in its workspace. It can start subagents from its agent definitions by name, and those subagents can start subagents of their own, which cannot start any. A remote agent running a skill works on its own. Where a skill would stop to ask the person, the parent's handoff tells it to decide and report what it decided at the end. For a stop point it cannot decide, such as a missing credential, the handoff says what to do, which can be asking the parent with the question tool. The plugin's skill teaches the parent to write that handoff. [sessions](../technical-design/sessions.md) covers how the skills and agents reach the remote agent.
    51	
    52	## ❓ Questions
    53	
    54	A remote agent can ask its parent a question when it needs a decision. The question can wait any length of time: the remote agent's work stays in its workspace while it waits.
    55	
    56	The plugin wakes the parent with the question itself. The parent can answer on its own or show the question to the person and answer when they reply, which can be much later. The parent answers with the answer tool, and the remote agent continues from where it asked. A prompt sent while a question waits does not answer the question; the prompt reaches the agent after the answer.
    57	
    58	Only the remote agent itself asks; subagents it starts inside its session cannot. [question-round-trip](../technical-design/question-round-trip.md) follows a question from the tool to the parent and back.
    59	
    60	## 🛑 Closing and reopening
    61	
    62	Closing a remote agent stops whatever it is doing. A closed agent leaves the status line but stays in the list, and its messages and status stay readable. A prompt to a closed agent reopens it and starts it working again.
    63	
    64	## 🗑️ Deleted remote agents
    65	
    66	tentacles deletes a remote agent a month after its last run stopped, whether it finished, failed or was closed. Reading its messages or status does not extend the month, and an agent that is working or waiting on a question is never deleted. Branches it pushed stay on GitHub; work it never pushed is deleted with it.
    67	
    68	tentacles does not tell the parent. The remote agent leaves the parent's list the first time the plugin notices: when the harness reopens the session, or when a call on the agent returns that the agent does not exist. Until then it can still appear in the list and the status line.
    69	
    70	## 🖼️ A preview for validation
    71	
    72	A remote agent can check the app it starts in a browser by opening a preview of it: a URL to its port on the preview domain, which carries a random token, together with a browser it drives with agent-browser. It opens the preview, checks what it built and closes it. An agent has one preview at a time; opening another replaces the open one. Other checks, such as calling an API, happen inside the agent's workspace with no preview. The preview closes when the agent's run stops, so it is the agent's way to check its own work, not something the parent or the person browses later. The remote agent has no browser for any other page.
    73

     6	
     7	# Question round trip
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	A remote agent asks its parent through its question tool, `ask_parent`, which waits inside the run. The session stores the question and moves to waiting, the session socket carries it to the plugin's helper, and the helper wakes the parent with the question itself. The parent answers, by itself or after asking the person behind it, and the answer resolves the waiting tool call so the run continues. Only the root conversation's model can ask, never a codemode script. The question waits as long as the parent takes: the workspace's files live with the session, so nothing the agent left unpushed is lost while it waits.
    12	
    13	## 📩 Flow
    14	
    15	```mermaid
    16	sequenceDiagram
    17	    autonumber
    18	    participant A as Remote agent
    19	    participant T as Question tool
    20	    participant S as Session
    21	    participant H as Plugin helper
    22	    participant P as Parent agent
    23	    actor Pe as Person
    24	    participant W as Worker
    25	    A->>T: asks
    26	    T->>S: store the question, move to waiting
    27	    S->>H: session state with the question
    28	    H->>P: wake with the question
    29	    opt the parent asks the person
    30	        P->>Pe: shows the question
    31	        Pe-->>P: the answer
    32	    end
    33	    P->>W: answer tool, by question id
    34	    W->>S: answer
    35	    S-->>A: the tool returns, the run continues
    36	```
    37	
    38	1. The agent calls the question tool.
    39	
    40	> [!NOTE] Only the root conversation asks
    41	> Subagent conversations inside the session do not get the question tool. A child conversation starts with a copy of its owner's extensions, and the question tool belongs to an extension only the root has. The subagent tool leaves that extension out of every copy. The parent reads only the root conversation, so a question from work it never sees would arrive without context.
    42	
    43	2. The session stores the question, its id and its text, and moves to waiting.
    44	3. The socket sends the session state with the question to the plugin's helper.
    45	4. The helper wakes the parent with the question itself: the session, the question id and the text, so the parent can answer without another call.
    46	5. and 6. The parent answers it itself, or shows it to the person and answers when they reply.
    47	7. and 8. The parent answers with the answer tool, by the question's id, through the Worker.
    48	9. The answer resolves the waiting tool call and the run continues. The socket sends the new state.
    49	
    50	A prompt sent while a question waits is a steer whatever mode the parent sends it with, and reaches the agent after the answer; a prompt neither answers nor cancels the question. A question keeps its id when an eviction makes the tool run again, so an answer sent for it still resolves it. Every eviction cuts the waiting tool call off, and pi-durable counts each cut-off toward its restart limit. The session lifts that limit while the question's call is live, so the question survives any number of evictions. An answer to a question that is not waiting returns an error, which the parent sees as a tool failure.
    51	
    52	> [!WARNING] No socket open when the question arrives
    53	> When the parent's helper is not connected (the harness is closed, or the parent runs headless), nothing wakes the parent. The question keeps waiting in the session and arrives with the state on the next connection; until then the run stays waiting and the session is never deleted.
    54

     7	# Plugin
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	The tentacles plugin gives a parent agent on pi or Claude Code one tool per action on its remote sessions: spawn, prompt, messages, wait (pi only), list, close and answer. It is built from one source into a pi package, published to npm, and a Claude plugin, published as a Claude Code marketplace. Each tool call runs a bundled helper CLI that calls the [Worker API](worker-api.md), and a long-running watch holds one socket per open session to update the status line and wake the parent when a session asks, finishes or fails. The plugin keeps a local list of the parent's remote sessions per harness session and syncs it with the Worker when the harness starts. It reaches tentacles only through the Worker API and the session sockets.
    12	
    13	## 🏗️ Architecture
    14	
    15	```mermaid
    16	flowchart LR

    55	
    56	The **harness glue** is a pi extension on pi and a Claude mod on Claude Code. It registers the tools, turns each tool call into a helper command, keeps the parent's local state, updates the status line and delivers the wakes.
    57	
    58	The **helper CLI** runs as one process per command, and as a long-running watch that holds one socket per open session in the local state and hands each state change back to the glue. For spawn it also stats the skill, agent and context paths the agent passed, reads only each SKILL.md and agent definition file to check them, checks that the context paths are files or folders with distinct names, and packs one archive per kind with a filesystem packer that reads the files as it packs (see [sessions](sessions.md)).     59	
    60	The **local state** is the parent's list of remote sessions, per harness session: a custom session entry on pi, a file under `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` on Claude Code. The glue reads it when the harness starts and writes it whenever the parent's sessions change.
    61	
    62	The **skill** teaches the parent agent the tools and adds that its children are remote: nothing of theirs runs locally, and their state and output are reachable only through the tools. It says that a session's skills and agent definitions are fixed at spawn, so the parent includes everything the job needs in the spawn, and spawns a new session when the job needs a different set. It also explains `context`: each path lands at `/workspace/context/<basename>`, outside the repository, as a copy fixed at spawn whose edits stay in the remote session and never come back, so the parent tells the remote agent in the handoff what the files are and how to use them. It tells the parent to write the handoff so the remote agent decides wherever a skill would stop for the user, ignores any instruction to ask the user, and lists those decisions in its final report. It also tells the parent to say in the handoff what to do at the stop points the agent cannot decide, such as a credential it lacks.
    63	
    64	## ♠️ What it exposes
    65	
    66	| Tool | On Claude Code (model sees) | On pi | Worker call |
    67	|---|---|---|---|
    68	| spawn | `mcp__tentacles__spawn` | `tentacles_spawn` | create |
    69	| prompt | `mcp__tentacles__prompt` | `tentacles_prompt` | prompt |
    70	| messages | `mcp__tentacles__messages` | `tentacles_messages` | messages |
    71	| wait | none | `tentacles_wait` | waits on the session socket |
    72	| list | `mcp__tentacles__list` | `tentacles_list` | list |
    73	| close | `mcp__tentacles__close` | `tentacles_close` | close |
    74	| answer | `mcp__tentacles__answer` | `tentacles_answer` | answer |
    75	
    76	Each tool takes the arguments of its Worker API call and returns its result, except where the plugin fills in the parent itself. spawn takes the name, the first prompt, any settings the agent sets, and optionally skill folder paths, agent definition paths and context file or folder paths; the plugin fills every other setting from its defaults (see Implementation details). When a skill, an agent definition or a context path fails a check, spawn returns every problem with its path, in a Skills, an Agents and a Context group, and creates nothing. list takes no arguments. A Worker error, such as a deleted or unknown session or an answer to a question that is not waiting, reaches the agent as a tool failure carrying the Worker's message. When the plugin gets no usable answer from the Worker, the tool fails with an error naming the cause: the Worker did not answer at its URL, it answered with an unexpected status, or a required variable is unset. On Claude Code the plugin registers the tools by their bare names and the model sees them under the plugin's MCP prefix; on pi they carry the `tentacles_` prefix themselves.

    78	> [!NOTE] Why Claude Code has no wait tool
    79	> The Claude mod runs every helper process with `$.process.run`, which Claude Code caps at ten minutes, so a wait could not block until a remote agent stops.     80	
    81	## ⏰ Wake messages
    82	
    83	The watch wakes the parent with what it needs to act without another call:
    84	
    85	| When | What the parent receives |
    86	|---|---|
    87	| a remote agent asks a question | the session, the question id and the question text |
    88	| a run finishes | the session and its last message |
    89	| a run fails | the session and its failure |
    90	
    91	[question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md) follows a question to the parent and back.
    92	
    93	On pi, a wake that arrives while the wait tool is waiting becomes the wait's result instead of a message. A wake that arrives while no wait is running goes out as a message, which pi holds until the parent's turn ends; the next wait returns that wake at once, unless the session has started running again since, and the wait after it waits for a new change.
    94	
    95	> [!NOTE] Why the next wait returns a wake that already went out
    96	> A wake can go out as a message while the parent's turn is still running, before the parent calls the wait. Returning it from the next wait keeps that wait from hanging on a change that already happened.
    97	
    98	> [!WARNING] A headless parent gets no wake

   128	The plugin keeps, per harness session, the parent's remote sessions with their name and status, closed ones included. The parent is identified by its harness and that harness's session id, which the Worker also stores on each session.
   129	
   130	When the harness starts and the local list is not empty, the plugin asks the Worker for the parent's sessions and replaces the list with the answer (1 to 3).      3	summary: "How a remote agent's question travels from its question tool to the parent agent, and how the answer resolves the waiting tool call."
     4	created: "2026-11-09"
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Question round trip
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	A remote agent asks its parent through its question tool, `ask_parent`, which waits inside the run. The session stores the question and moves to waiting, the session socket carries it to the plugin's helper, and the helper wakes the parent with the question itself. The parent answers, by itself or after asking the person behind it, and the answer resolves the waiting tool call so the run continues. Only the root conversation's model can ask, never a codemode script. The question waits as long as the parent takes: the workspace's files live with the session, so nothing the agent left unpushed is lost while it waits.
    12	
    13	## 📩 Flow
    14	
    15	```mermaid
    16	sequenceDiagram
    17	    autonumber
    18	    participant A as Remote agent
    19	    participant T as Question tool
    20	    participant S as Session
    21	    participant H as Plugin helper
    22	    participant P as Parent agent
    23	    actor Pe as Person
    24	    participant W as Worker
    25	    A->>T: asks
    26	    T->>S: store the question, move to waiting
    27	    S->>H: session state with the question
    28	    H->>P: wake with the question
    29	    opt the parent asks the person
    30	        P->>Pe: shows the question
    31	        Pe-->>P: the answer
    32	    end
    33	    P->>W: answer tool, by question id
    34	    W->>S: answer
    35	    S-->>A: the tool returns, the run continues
    36	```
    37	
    38	1. The agent calls the question tool.
    39	
    40	> [!NOTE] Only the root conversation asks
    41	> Subagent conversations inside the session do not get the question tool. A child conversation starts with a copy of its owner's extensions, and the question tool belongs to an extension only the root has. The subagent tool leaves that extension out of every copy. The parent reads only the root conversation, so a question from work it never sees would arrive without context.
    42	
    43	2. The session stores the question, its id and its text, and moves to waiting.
    44	3. The socket sends the session state with the question to the plugin's helper.
    45	4. The helper wakes the parent with the question itself: the session, the question id and the text, so the parent can answer without another call.
    46	5. and 6. The parent answers it itself, or shows it to the person and answers when they reply.
    47	7. and 8. The parent answers with the answer tool, by the question's id, through the Worker.
    48	9. The answer resolves the waiting tool call and the run continues. The socket sends the new state.
    49	
    50	A prompt sent while a question waits is a steer whatever mode the parent sends it with, and reaches the agent after the answer; a prompt neither answers nor cancels the question. A question keeps its id when an eviction makes the tool run again, so an answer sent for it still resolves it. Every eviction cuts the waiting tool call off, and pi-durable counts each cut-off toward its restart limit. The session lifts that limit while the question's call is live, so the question survives any number of evictions. An answer to a question that is not waiting returns an error, which the parent sees as a tool failure.
    51	
    52	> [!WARNING] No socket open when the question arrives
    53	> When the parent's helper is not connected (the harness is closed, or the parent runs headless), nothing wakes the parent. The question keeps waiting in the session and arrives with the state on the next connection; until then the run stays waiting and the session is never deleted.
    54

     2	title: "Remote agents"
     3	summary: "What it is like for a parent agent, and the person behind it, to dispatch coding agents that run on Cloudflare and follow them through tentacles."
     4	created: "2026-11-09"
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Remote agents
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	tentacles lets an agent on pi or Claude Code start coding agents that run remotely, on Cloudflare, and work with them the way it works with local subagents: spawn them, prompt and steer them, see when they stop, answer their questions and close them. The parent agent does all of it through a set of tools; nothing of a remote agent runs on the developer's machine. When the parent goes away, a remote agent keeps working and waits on its questions, and the parent finds it when it comes back. Its work stays in its workspace for as long as the remote agent exists: what it pushes survives the remote agent's deletion, and what it does not push goes with the remote agent a month after its last run. Every commit a remote agent makes is authored by the name and email the deploy sets, whoever spawned the agent.
    12	
    13	## 🚀 Spawning a remote agent
    14	
    15	The parent spawns a remote agent with a name, a first prompt and its settings: the provider, the model, the effort level, the container image and size, and optionally a repository to work on. The name is required; the status line and the list show the remote agent by its name. Any setting the parent leaves out takes the plugin's default, which the person can change through environment variables. Spawn answers once the remote agent's workspace is set up, with the repository cloned and its skills and context in place, and the agent then starts working on the first prompt. When the setup fails, spawn returns the reason, such as a repository URL that does not exist or a token that cannot read the repository, and spawn leaves the remote agent failed with that reason; it never starts working.
    16	
    17	With a repository in its settings, the remote agent starts with it cloned. Without one, it clones whatever its prompt names. Claude models run on the person's own Claude subscription, and models from other providers are available too.
    18	
    19	[workspace](../technical-design/workspace.md) covers the workspace's setup, its tools and what survives a container stop.
    20	
    21	The parent can also give the remote agent skills and agent definitions, by passing their folder and file paths at spawn. They are fixed for the remote agent's life, so the parent includes every one the job needs, and work that needs a different set goes to a new remote agent. The plugin checks every skill and agent definition on the developer's machine before anything is sent; when one fails, spawn returns every problem with its path, skills, agents and context listed apart, and no remote agent starts.
    22	
    23	The parent can also send context files, the files and folders on its machine that the repository does not hold, such as a change's scratch files, by passing their paths at spawn. The remote agent finds each one in `/workspace/context` under its own name, outside the repository. The copy is fixed at spawn: the remote agent can change it, but its changes stay in its workspace and never come back to the parent, so work that needs different files goes to a new remote agent. The remote agent is told only that the parent sent files and that they are in `/workspace/context`, so the parent says in its handoff what the files are and how to use them. Two paths with the same name, a path that does not exist, or files that pack over 5 MB fail the spawn in the Context group. [sessions](../technical-design/sessions.md) covers how the context reaches the remote agent.
    24	
    25	## 💬 Prompting and steering
    26	
    27	While a remote agent works, the parent can send it a prompt as a follow-up, which the agent takes up after its current turn, or as a steer, which redirects it mid-run. A prompt to an agent that has finished starts it working again.
    28	
    29	Nobody watches a remote agent live. The parent reads what it did through the messages tool: its last message by default, or the last N, where a message is any entry of its conversation (prompts, its text, tool calls and results, subagent results). On pi, the parent can also block on a remote agent with the wait tool.
    30	
    31	A prompt can name one of the remote agent's skills, as `/skill:<name>` or `/<name>` standing on its own, with a space or the start or end of the prompt on each side. The remote agent receives a short block in its place that points at the skill's instructions, and reads the instructions before acting on the skill. A name the remote agent does not hold, or one inside a path or with punctuation attached, stays as written.
    32	
    33	## 📊 The status line
    34	
    35	The harness shows a status line with the name and status of each open remote agent: running, waiting on a question, idle or failed. The status line hides closed ones, but the list tool still returns them.
    36	
    37	The list belongs to the parent's harness session. When the harness reopens that session, the plugin refreshes the list from tentacles, so the status line shows each agent's current status, including changes made while the parent was away. A forked parent starts with no remote agents of its own.
    38	
    39	The list also returns each remote agent's settings and the names of its skills and agents, so a parent that comes back later knows what each remote agent can do.
    40	
    41	## ⏰ Finish and failure wakes
    42	
    43	When a remote agent's run finishes, the plugin wakes the parent with that agent's last message, so the parent can read the result without another call. When a run fails on an error the agent cannot recover from, the plugin wakes the parent with the failure. In both cases the remote agent stays available: a prompt starts it on a new run.
    44	
    45	> [!WARNING] A headless parent is never woken
    46	> A parent running headless (`claude -p`) gets no wake, as with local subagents. It learns that a remote agent finished or asked something only by calling the tools.
    47	
    48	## 🧩 Skills and agents inside a remote agent
    49	
    50	A remote agent sees its skills and agent definitions by name and description, and loads a skill when a task matches it, reading its instructions and the files they point to. It installs whatever a skill needs to run in its workspace. It can start subagents from its agent definitions by name, and those subagents can start subagents of their own, which cannot start any. A remote agent running a skill works on its own. Where a skill would stop to ask the person, the parent's handoff tells it to decide and report what it decided at the end. For a stop point it cannot decide, such as a missing credential, the handoff says what to do, which can be asking the parent with the question tool. The plugin's skill teaches the parent to write that handoff. [sessions](../technical-design/sessions.md) covers how the skills and agents reach the remote agent.
    51	
    52	## ❓ Questions
    53	
    54	A remote agent can ask its parent a question when it needs a decision. The question can wait any length of time: the remote agent's work stays in its workspace while it waits.
    55	
    56	The plugin wakes the parent with the question itself. The parent can answer on its own or show the question to the person and answer when they reply, which can be much later. The parent answers with the answer tool, and the remote agent continues from where it asked. A prompt sent while a question waits does not answer the question; the prompt reaches the agent after the answer.
    57	
    58	Only the remote agent itself asks; subagents it starts inside its session cannot. [question-round-trip](../technical-design/question-round-trip.md) follows a question from the tool to the parent and back.
    59	
    60	## 🛑 Closing and reopening
    61	
    62	Closing a remote agent stops whatever it is doing. A closed agent leaves the status line but stays in the list, and its messages and status stay readable. A prompt to a closed agent reopens it and starts it working again.
    63	
    64	## 🗑️ Deleted remote agents
    65	
    66	tentacles deletes a remote agent a month after its last run stopped, whether it finished, failed or was closed. Reading its messages or status does not extend the month, and an agent that is working or waiting on a question is never deleted. Branches it pushed stay on GitHub; work it never pushed is deleted with it.
    67	
    68	tentacles does not tell the parent. The remote agent leaves the parent's list the first time the plugin notices: when the harness reopens the session, or when a call on the agent returns that the agent does not exist. Until then it can still appear in the list and the status line.
    69	
    70	## 🖼️ A preview for validation
    71	
    72	A remote agent can check the app it starts in a browser by opening a preview of it: a URL to its port on the preview domain, which carries a random token, together with a browser it drives with agent-browser. It opens the preview, checks what it built and closes it. An agent has one preview at a time; opening another replaces the open one. Other checks, such as calling an API, happen inside the agent's workspace with no preview. The preview closes when the agent's run stops, so it is the agent's way to check its own work, not something the parent or the person browses later. The remote agent has no browser for any other page.
    73	
    74	---
    75

    55	
    56	The **harness glue** is a pi extension on pi and a Claude mod on Claude Code. It registers the tools, turns each tool call into a helper command, keeps the parent's local state, updates the status line and delivers the wakes.
    57	
    58	The **helper CLI** runs as one process per command, and as a long-running watch that holds one socket per open session in the local state and hands each state change back to the glue. It reads the Worker URL and the API key from environment variables, and the default session settings come from environment variables too (see Implementation details).
    59	
    60	The **local state** is the parent's list of remote sessions, per harness session: a custom session entry on pi, a file under `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` on Claude Code. The glue reads it when the harness starts and writes it whenever the parent's sessions change.
    61	
    62	The **skill** teaches the parent agent the tools and adds that its children are remote: nothing of theirs runs locally, and their state and output are reachable only through the tools. It says that a session's skills and agent definitions are fixed at spawn, so the parent includes everything the job needs in the spawn, and spawns a new session when the job needs a different set. It also explains `context`: each path lands at `/workspace/context/<basename>`, outside the repository, as a copy fixed at spawn whose edits stay in the remote session and never come back, so the parent tells the remote agent in the handoff what the files are and how to use them. It tells the parent to write the handoff so the remote agent decides wherever a skill would stop for the user, ignores any instruction to ask the user, and lists those decisions in its final report. It also tells the parent to say in the handoff what to do at the stop points the agent cannot decide, such as a credential it lacks.
    63	
    64	## ♠️ What it exposes
    65	
    66	| Tool | On Claude Code (model sees) | On pi | Worker call |
    67	|---|---|---|---|
    68	| spawn | `mcp__tentacles__spawn` | `tentacles_spawn` | create |
    69	| prompt | `mcp__tentacles__prompt` | `tentacles_prompt` | prompt |
    70	| messages | `mcp__tentacles__messages` | `tentacles_messages` | messages |
    71	| wait | none | `tentacles_wait` | waits on the session socket |
    72	| list | `mcp__tentacles__list` | `tentacles_list` | list |
    73	| close | `mcp__tentacles__close` | `tentacles_close` | close |
    74	| answer | `mcp__tentacles__answer` | `tentacles_answer` | answer |
    75	
    76	Each tool takes the arguments of its Worker API call and returns its result, except where the plugin fills in the parent itself. spawn takes the name, the first prompt, any settings the agent sets, and optionally skill folder paths, agent definition paths and context file or folder paths; the plugin fills every other setting from its defaults (see Implementation details). When the plugin gets no usable answer from the Worker, the tool fails with an error naming the cause: the Worker did not answer at its URL, it answered with an unexpected status, or a required variable is unset.     80	
    81	## ⏰ Wake messages
    82	
    83	The watch wakes the parent with what it needs to act without another call:

    85	| When | What the parent receives |
    86	|---|---|
    87	| a remote agent asks a question | the session, the question id and the question text |
    88	| a run finishes | the session and its last message |
    89	| a run fails | the session and its failure |
    90	
    91	[question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md) follows a question to the parent and back.
    92	
    93	On pi, a wake that arrives while the wait tool is waiting becomes the wait's result instead of a message.     94	
    95	> [!NOTE] Why the next wait returns a wake that already went out
    96	> A wake can go out as a message while the parent's turn is still running, before the parent calls the wait. Returning it from the next wait keeps that wait from hanging on a change that already happened.
    97	
    98	> [!WARNING] A headless parent gets no wake
    99	> A parent running headless (`claude -p`) is never woken, the same as with local subagents. It learns of a question or a finished run only by calling the tools, and a question it never reads keeps its session waiting.

   127	
   128	The plugin keeps, per harness session, the parent's remote sessions with their name and status, closed ones included. The parent is identified by its harness and that harness's session id, which the Worker also stores on each session.
   129	
   130	When the harness starts and the local list is not empty, the plugin asks the Worker for the parent's sessions and replaces the list with the answer (1 to 3). With an empty list, the plugin makes no call. A forked parent (pi's `/fork`, Claude Code's `/branch` or `--fork-session`) has a new session id, so its first sync returns nothing and its list empties: a fork sees none of the original's remote sessions.
   131	
   132	spawn adds a session, close marks it closed, and a prompt that reopens a closed session marks it open again (4, 5). The watch holds a socket for each open session in the list, and every state event updates that session's status (6, 7).    133
