   137	
   138	> [!NOTE] Why the list is kept both locally and in the Worker
   139	> The local list lets a harness that has never spawned a remote session start without calling the Worker. The Worker's copy lets a harness that does have sessions recover their current status, including changes it missed while it was closed.
   140	
   141	> [!WARNING] A deleted session lingers until the plugin learns of it
   142	> The daily cleanup deletes a session without telling its parent. The local list still names the session, and so does the status line if the session was open. This lasts until the next start-up sync, the next call on the session, or, for an open session, the watch's next connection to it.
   143	
   144	## 📦 Publishing and installing

     3	summary: "How a remote agent's question travels from its question tool to the parent agent, and how the answer resolves the waiting tool call."
     4	created: "2026-11-09"
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Question round trip
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	A remote agent asks its parent through its question tool, `ask_parent`, which waits inside the run. The session stores the question and moves to waiting, the session socket carries it to the plugin's helper, and the helper wakes the parent with the question itself. The parent answers, by itself or after asking the person behind it, and the answer resolves the waiting tool call so the run continues. Only the root conversation's model can ask, never a codemode script. The question waits as long as the parent takes: the workspace's files live with the session, so nothing the agent left unpushed is lost while it waits.
    12	
    13	## 📩 Flow
    14	
    15	```mermaid
    16	sequenceDiagram
    17	    autonumber
    18	    participant A as Remote agent
    19	    participant T as Question tool
    20	    participant S as Session
    21	    participant H as Plugin helper
    22	    participant P as Parent agent
    23	    actor Pe as Person
    24	    participant W as Worker
    25	    A->>T: asks
    26	    T->>S: store the question, move to waiting
    27	    S->>H: session state with the question
    28	    H->>P: wake with the question
    29	    opt the parent asks the person
    30	        P->>Pe: shows the question
    31	        Pe-->>P: the answer
    32	    end
    33	    P->>W: answer tool, by question id
    34	    W->>S: answer
    35	    S-->>A: the tool returns, the run continues
    36	```
    37	
    38	1. The agent calls the question tool.
    39	
    40	> [!NOTE] Only the root conversation asks
    41	> Subagent conversations inside the session do not get the question tool. A child conversation starts with a copy of its owner's extensions, and the question tool belongs to an extension only the root has. The subagent tool leaves that extension out of every copy. The parent reads only the root conversation, so a question from work it never sees would arrive without context.
    42	
    43	2. The session stores the question, its id and its text, and moves to waiting.
    44	3. The socket sends the session state with the question to the plugin's helper.
    45	4. The helper wakes the parent with the question itself: the session, the question id and the text, so the parent can answer without another call.
    46	5. and 6. The parent answers it itself, or shows it to the person and answers when they reply.
    47	7. and 8. The parent answers with the answer tool, by the question's id, through the Worker.
    48	9. The answer resolves the waiting tool call and the run continues. The socket sends the new state.
    49	
    50	A prompt sent while a question waits is a steer whatever mode the parent sends it with, and reaches the agent after the answer; a prompt neither answers nor cancels the question. A question keeps its id when an eviction makes the tool run again, so an answer sent for it still resolves it. Every eviction cuts the waiting tool call off, and pi-durable counts each cut-off toward its restart limit. The session lifts that limit while the question's call is live, so the question survives any number of evictions. An answer to a question that is not waiting returns an error, which the parent sees as a tool failure.
    51	
    52	> [!WARNING] No socket open when the question arrives
    53	> When the parent's helper is not connected (the harness is closed, or the parent runs headless), nothing wakes the parent. The question keeps waiting in the session and arrives with the state on the next connection; until then the run stays waiting and the session is never deleted.
    54	
    55	---

     1	---
     2	title: "Remote agents"
     3	summary: "What it is like for a parent agent, and the person behind it, to dispatch coding agents that run on Cloudflare and follow them through tentacles."
     4	created: "2026-11-09"
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Remote agents
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	tentacles lets an agent on pi or Claude Code start coding agents that run remotely, on Cloudflare, and work with them the way it works with local subagents: spawn them, prompt and steer them, see when they stop, answer their questions and close them. The parent agent does all of it through a set of tools; nothing of a remote agent runs on the developer's machine. When the parent goes away, a remote agent keeps working and waits on its questions, and the parent finds it when it comes back. Its work stays in its workspace for as long as the remote agent exists: what it pushes survives the remote agent's deletion, and what it does not push goes with the remote agent a month after its last run. Every commit a remote agent makes is authored by the name and email the deploy sets, whoever spawned the agent.
    12	
    13	## 🚀 Spawning a remote agent
    14	
    15	The parent spawns a remote agent with a name, a first prompt and its settings: the provider, the model, the effort level, the container image and size, and optionally a repository to work on. The name is required; the status line and the list show the remote agent by its name. Any setting the parent leaves out takes the plugin's default, which the person can change through environment variables. Spawn answers once the remote agent's workspace is set up, with the repository cloned and its skills and context in place, and the agent then starts working on the first prompt. When the setup fails, spawn returns the reason, such as a repository URL that does not exist or a token that cannot read the repository, and spawn leaves the remote agent failed with that reason; it never starts working.
    16	
    17	With a repository in its settings, the remote agent starts with it cloned. Without one, it clones whatever its prompt names. Claude models run on the person's own Claude subscription, and models from other providers are available too.
    18	
    19	[workspace](../technical-design/workspace.md) covers the workspace's setup, its tools and what survives a container stop.
    20	
    21	The parent can also give the remote agent skills and agent definitions, by passing their folder and file paths at spawn. They are fixed for the remote agent's life, so the parent includes every one the job needs, and work that needs a different set goes to a new remote agent. The plugin checks every skill and agent definition on the developer's machine before anything is sent; when one fails, spawn returns every problem with its path, skills, agents and context listed apart, and no remote agent starts.
    22	
    23	The parent can also send context files, the files and folders on its machine that the repository does not hold, such as a change's scratch files, by passing their paths at spawn. The remote agent finds each one in `/workspace/context` under its own name, outside the repository. The copy is fixed at spawn: the remote agent can change it, but its changes stay in its workspace and never come back to the parent, so work that needs different files goes to a new remote agent. The remote agent is told only that the parent sent files and that they are in `/workspace/context`, so the parent says in its handoff what the files are and how to use them. Two paths with the same name, a path that does not exist, or files that pack over 5 MB fail the spawn in the Context group. [sessions](../technical-design/sessions.md) covers how the context reaches the remote agent.
    24	
    25	## 💬 Prompting and steering
    26	
    27	While a remote agent works, the parent can send it a prompt as a follow-up, which the agent takes up after its current turn, or as a steer, which redirects it mid-run. A prompt to an agent that has finished starts it working again.
    28	
    29	Nobody watches a remote agent live. The parent reads what it did through the messages tool: its last message by default, or the last N, where a message is any entry of its conversation (prompts, its text, tool calls and results, subagent results). On pi, the parent can also block on a remote agent with the wait tool.
    30	
    31	A prompt can name one of the remote agent's skills, as `/skill:<name>` or `/<name>` standing on its own, with a space or the start or end of the prompt on each side. The remote agent receives a short block in its place that points at the skill's instructions, and reads the instructions before acting on the skill. A name the remote agent does not hold, or one inside a path or with punctuation attached, stays as written.
    32	
    33	## 📊 The status line
    34	
    35	The harness shows a status line with the name and status of each open remote agent: running, waiting on a question, idle or failed. The status line hides closed ones, but the list tool still returns them.
    36	
    37	The list belongs to the parent's harness session. When the harness reopens that session, the plugin refreshes the list from tentacles, so the status line shows each agent's current status, including changes made while the parent was away. A forked parent starts with no remote agents of its own.
    38	
    39	The list also returns each remote agent's settings and the names of its skills and agents, so a parent that comes back later knows what each remote agent can do.
    40	
    41	## ⏰ Finish and failure wakes
    42	
    43	When a remote agent's run finishes, the plugin wakes the parent with that agent's last message, so the parent can read the result without another call. When a run fails on an error the agent cannot recover from, the plugin wakes the parent with the failure. In both cases the remote agent stays available: a prompt starts it on a new run.
    44	
    45	> [!WARNING] A headless parent is never woken
    46	> A parent running headless (`claude -p`) gets no wake, as with local subagents. It learns that a remote agent finished or asked something only by calling the tools.
    47	
    48	## 🧩 Skills and agents inside a remote agent
    49	
    50	A remote agent sees its skills and agent definitions by name and description, and loads a skill when a task matches it, reading its instructions and the files they point to. It installs whatever a skill needs to run in its workspace. It can start subagents from its agent definitions by name, and those subagents can start subagents of their own, which cannot start any. A remote agent running a skill works on its own. Where a skill would stop to ask the person, the parent's handoff tells it to decide and report what it decided at the end. For a stop point it cannot decide, such as a missing credential, the handoff says what to do, which can be asking the parent with the question tool. The plugin's skill teaches the parent to write that handoff. [sessions](../technical-design/sessions.md) covers how the skills and agents reach the remote agent.
    51	
    52	## ❓ Questions
    53	
    54	A remote agent can ask its parent a question when it needs a decision. The question can wait any length of time: the remote agent's work stays in its workspace while it waits.
    55	
    56	The plugin wakes the parent with the question itself. The parent can answer on its own or show the question to the person and answer when they reply, which can be much later. The parent answers with the answer tool, and the remote agent continues from where it asked. A prompt sent while a question waits does not answer the question; the prompt reaches the agent after the answer.
    57	
    58	Only the remote agent itself asks; subagents it starts inside its session cannot. [question-round-trip](../technical-design/question-round-trip.md) follows a question from the tool to the parent and back.
    59	
    60	## 🛑 Closing and reopening
    61	
    62	Closing a remote agent stops whatever it is doing. A closed agent leaves the status line but stays in the list, and its messages and status stay readable. A prompt to a closed agent reopens it and starts it working again.
    63	
    64	## 🗑️ Deleted remote agents
    65	
    66	tentacles deletes a remote agent a month after its last run stopped, whether it finished, failed or was closed. Reading its messages or status does not extend the month, and an agent that is working or waiting on a question is never deleted. Branches it pushed stay on GitHub; work it never pushed is deleted with it.
    67	
    68	tentacles does not tell the parent. The remote agent leaves the parent's list the first time the plugin notices: when the harness reopens the session, or when a call on the agent returns that the agent does not exist. Until then it can still appear in the list and the status line.
    69	
    70	## 🖼️ A preview for validation
    71	
    72	A remote agent can check the app it starts in a browser by opening a preview of it: a URL to its port on the preview domain, which carries a random token, together with a browser it drives with agent-browser. It opens the preview, checks what it built and closes it. An agent has one preview at a time; opening another replaces the open one. Other checks, such as calling an API, happen inside the agent's workspace with no preview. The preview closes when the agent's run stops, so it is the agent's way to check its own work, not something the parent or the person browses later. The remote agent has no browser for any other page.
    73	
    74	---
    75

     7	# Cloudflare workspace
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	On Cloudflare, a session's workspace is a Cloudflare Computer workspace that lives in the session's Durable Object. Its files sit in the object's SQLite and are mounted into the container at `/workspace`, at the same paths on both sides. The agent gets Computer's tools: file tools that work on the object's files directly, and `exec`, which runs a command on the isolate shell or the container. One git client per workspace, with a fetch that adds the GitHub token, serves clone, fetch and push from the object, the shell and codemode; git run inside the container reaches GitHub through the egress gateway, which adds the token there. Computer and the platform run the container's lifecycle: it starts on the first command sent to it and stops when idle.
    12	
    13	## 🖥️ The backends and what each can run
    14	
    15	[Workspace](../../workspace.md) draws how a tool call reaches the files and the backends.
    16	
    17	The workspace registers two backends, and `exec`'s `backend` parameter names one of them on each call:
    18	
    19	| Backend | What it is | What it can run | Output |
    20	|---|---|---|---|
    21	| shell | just-bash in a Dynamic Worker, on the Durable Object's files | text tools such as grep, sed, sort and tar, and `git`, which forwards to the workspace git client; no node, npm or other binaries | the whole output when the command ends |
    22	| container | a Cloudflare container running computerd, with the Durable Object's files mounted at `/workspace` | anything the image holds or the agent installs: node, npm, mise, real git, servers for a preview | each line as it is printed, from Computer's exec event stream |
    23	
    24	The file tools, `read`, `ls`, `find`, `grep`, `write`, `edit` and `delete`, take no backend and work on the Durable Object's files. The provider sets `read`, `ls`, `find` and `grep` to replay safe and `write`, `edit`, `delete` and `exec` to unsafe.
    25	
    26	The provider writes each backend's description, which Computer puts in front of its own text, so the agent picks a backend from what the real setup can do. Where Computer's built-in text does not match the setup, such as the shell's "no direct network", the provider's description corrects it. The provider leaves long commands on the shell, and their output comes back when they end.
    27	
    28	`exec` hands the harness each stdout and stderr event in the order it arrives, then the result with the command, the exit code and the full output. Computer reports a non-zero exit as a success, so the provider sets the error flag itself when the exit code is not 0.
    29	
    30	> [!NOTE] Why the shell's output arrives only at the end
    31	> Computer's shell backend awaits just-bash's `exec` to completion and builds its event stream from the finished result, and just-bash has no output callback. A container command streams; a shell command cannot.
    32	
    33	## 📂 `/workspace` in the Durable Object
    34	
    35	The workspace's files live in the session Durable Object's SQLite, next to pi-durable's tables. computerd mounts them in the container at `/workspace` through FUSE, so `/workspace/repo`, `/workspace/skills` and `/workspace/context` have the same paths for the file tools, the shell and the container. Only `/workspace` is shared: anything the container writes elsewhere sits on the container's own disk and is lost when the container stops. The runtimes mise installs live outside `/workspace`, so the agent installs them again after a stop.
    36	
    37	`node_modules` and every other tree an install writes under `/workspace` sync into the Durable Object like any other file, and the agent's instructions do not mention it.
    38	
    39	> [!NOTE] Why `node_modules` stays in the synced workspace
    40	> Keeping it on the container's disk would hide it from the file tools and the shell, and a stop would lose it. Syncing costs install time instead: an npm install took 11.4 s synced against 4.8 s on the container's disk.
    41	
    42	At spawn, the provider builds the workspace and runs the setup without starting a container: it clones the repository into `/workspace/repo` through the git client and writes the skills and context archives' files into `/workspace/skills` and `/workspace/context` through the workspace's file system. Deleting the session clears the Durable Object's storage, and the workspace's files with it.
    43	
    44	## 🔀 Git and egress
    45	
    46	```mermaid
    47	flowchart LR
    48	  ag@{ shape: rect, label: "Agent" }
    49	  so@{ shape: subproc, label: "Workspace git client
    50	  (session object)" }

    52	  ct@{ shape: rect, label: "Container" }
    53	  gw@{ shape: rect, label: "Egress gateway" }
    54	  gh@{ shape: rect, label: "github.com" }
    55	  oh@{ shape: rect, label: "Other hosts" }
    56	  so -->|"1 clone at setup, token added by the git fetch"| gh
    57	  ag -->|"2 git in the shell"| sh
    58	  sh -->|"3 forwards to the workspace git client"| so

    60	  ag -->|"5 git, npm, curl in the container"| ct
    61	  ct -->|"6 every request, interception CA trusted"| gw

    63	  gw -->|"8 passed unchanged"| oh
    64	  classDef worker fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1f2937
    65	  classDef flow fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937

    71	
    72	The workspace git client clones at setup (1). Git run in the isolate shell (2) forwards to the same client (3), whose fetch adds the GitHub token (4); codemode scripts' git goes through the same client. Anything the agent runs in the container (5) goes through the egress gateway (6), which adds the token on github.com (7) and passes other hosts unchanged (8).
    73	
    74	The egress gateway is Computer's `http-gateway` mode, fixed by the provider: every outbound request from the container is intercepted and handed to the gateway, which lets all traffic through and adds the token only on github.com. The token never enters the container, its git config or its remote URLs.
    75	
    76	The container trusts the gateway's interception certificate before the agent's first command runs. Cloudflare writes that certificate into the container only after the container starts, and computerd passes exec'd commands nothing but `HOME`, `PATH` and the working directory, so the image installs the certificate into the system trust store once it appears. curl, git, npm and node's fetch then accept the intercepted connections.
    77	
    78	The identity from create is set on the git client as its default identity and in the environment of every container command, as `GIT_AUTHOR_*` and `GIT_COMMITTER_*`. The two routes read different sources, so the provider sets both.
    79	
    80	> [!TIP] Rejected: cloning and pushing with git in the container
    81	> Container git needs the container started and the interception certificate trusted, and pays a cold start before the first command. The git client in the Durable Object clones in under a second with no container, keeps the token outside every backend, and leaves container git to what the agent runs there.
    82	
    83	## 📦 The image
    84	
    85	The container runs the workspace image with Computer's daemon added: computerd and FUSE, on top of what the agent needs to install its own toolchain in any language: git, CA certificates, `curl`, `xz`, `unzip`, `bzip2`, `ps` and the `libatomic` library that prebuilt Node binaries load. It also holds mise, a runtime manager that installs Node, Python, Go and other runtimes on demand, as in `mise use node@24`, with mise's shims directory on `PATH`. The image has no preinstalled language runtime, no Chrome and no Docker; the agent installs anything else it needs. The image's name is the `default` value of the session's image setting, and the size setting picks the container's instance type.
    86	
    87	> [!WARNING] Agent commands can read computerd's secret
    88	> computerd's environment, including its `RPC_CLIENT_SECRET`, is readable from `/proc/1/environ` by any command the agent runs. The secret only lets a caller drive the same container the agent already controls, so the provider accepts it.
    89	
    90	## 🟢 The container's lifecycle
    91	
    92	Computer and the platform run the container; the provider has no start, stop or keepalive call. The first command sent to the container starts it, Computer restarts it if computerd does not come up, and Cloudflare Containers stops it once the Durable Object has been idle. A stop keeps `/workspace` and loses the running processes, including servers started for a preview, and anything outside `/workspace`. A cold start with the image cached takes about 1 to 3 seconds before the first command runs.
    93

tentacles runs the pi-durable `Harness` inside one Cloudflare Durable Object per session. A local pi or Claude Code plugin reaches it through an HTTP API and a WebSocket, using tools that call a helper CLI. The agent loop, its state and its tools all run remotely; nothing of a remote agent runs on the developer's machine.

Docs paths are under `/home/agus/workspace/asermax/tentacles/docs/`. Code paths are under `/home/agus/workspace/asermax/tentacles/`.

**1. Parts and connections**
- **Plugin** (`apps/plugin`, one source built into the pi package `@asermax/pi-tentacles` and a Claude plugin; `technical-design/plugin.md:11,56-60`).
  - Harness glue is a pi extension (`src/pi/extension.ts`) or a Claude mod (`src/claude/engine.ts`). It registers one tool per action: spawn, prompt, messages, list, close, answer, plus wait on pi only.
  - The helper CLI (`src/helper/*`) runs one process per command. A `watch` process holds one WebSocket per open session.
- **Worker** (`packages/provider-cloudflare/src/worker.ts`).
  - The only entry point. It serves the `/api` HTTP API (`packages/worker-api/src/api.ts:5`) behind a `TENTACLES_API_KEY` check (`worker.ts:72-86`), and also the preview route and a cron trigger.
  - The plugin-facing calls are create, prompt, answer, close, messages, status and list, plus a per-session socket (`technical-design/worker-api.md:11-24`). Payloads are JSON, and create carries base64 gzip-tar archives for skills, agents and context, up to 5 MB each (`worker-api.md:40-44`).
  - The socket sends one construct, the session state (status, settings, skill and agent names, question, failure, last entry), on connect and on every change (`worker-api.md:56`).
- **Registry Durable Object** (`registry-object.ts`, `packages/sql-registry`). It holds one entry per session (id, name, parent harness and id, status, `last_stopped`, settings, preview token). It serves list and preview lookups and feeds the daily cleanup (`sessions.md:136-140`).
- **Session Durable Object** (`session-object.ts:51`). It is keyed by session id and fills five contracts: SessionHost, SessionStorage, WakeTimer, ParentChannel and Workspace (`providers/cloudflare/deploy.md:73`). It reports each status change to the registry.
- **Workspace container**: a Cloudflare Computer container running computerd, started on the first command sent to it.
- **Shared Claude container** (`claude-object.ts`, `apps/claude-relay`): one container for all sessions, running pi-claude-code's relay and the claude CLI. It stops 15 minutes after the last call (`claude-object.ts:16`).
- **Other parts**: Codemode Worker (QuickJS sandbox Durable Object), Browser Run for previews, AI Gateway for non-Claude models, and a cron trigger (`deploy.md:75-107`).
- **Contracts**: the provider-neutral roles live in `packages/contracts/src/*`. A provider fills each one (`technical-design/runtime-components.md:64-83`).

**2. Agent loop, state, persistence, resume**
- The loop runs in the session Durable Object. `packages/core/src/session/session.ts:117` calls `Harness.open(storage, { models, registry, settings, onWake, env })`.
- State lives in pi-durable's SQLite tables inside that Durable Object (`session-object.ts:106`, `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage`). Conversations are pi-durable's own. tentacles adds a SESSION record, a questions document, and skills, agents and context documents (`sessions.md:62-134`). The workspace files live in the same SQLite (`providers/cloudflare/computer-workspace.md:35`).
- Status is derived from pi-durable state and is not a stored field (`sessions.md:131`, `core/src/session/state.ts`). The registry entry is a projection of it.
- Resume after an eviction goes through pi-durable's `onWake` and the Durable Object alarm (`session.ts:133`, `session-object.ts:216` `alarm: () => handle.wake()`). The alarm is reserved for pi-durable (`invariants.md:24`).
- Tools with `replay: "safe"` are rerun after an eviction. The workspace sets reads to safe and `write`, `edit`, `delete` and `exec` to unsafe (`workspace.md:98`, `computer-workspace.md:24`).
- A waiting question keeps its id across replays. `restartLimit` is `Infinity` while the question's call is live (`session.ts:127-131`), so it survives any number of evictions (`question-round-trip.md:50`).
- A daily cron deletes sessions whose last run stopped over a month ago, clearing the Durable Object storage and then the registry entry (`sessions.md:411-445`).

**3. Tools, dispatch, steer, question, collect**
- **Tool installation**: `packages/core/src/tools/extension.ts:55` installs pi-durable's `CodingTools`, codemode, the commit check, the preview tool, skills, context, agents and the root-only `ask_parent`. The `Workspace` contract's `create` returns pi-durable ToolRegistrations, each with its own `execute` (`workspace.md:98`).
- **Where the shell and filesystem are** (`computer-workspace.md:17-35`):
  - File tools work directly on the Durable Object's SQLite.
  - `exec` runs either on an isolate shell (just-bash in a Dynamic Worker, text tools and `git` only) or in the container. The container mounts `/workspace` through FUSE.
  - Only `/workspace` persists across a container stop.
  - Git clones and pushes from the Durable Object, and GitHub tokens are added outside the container, by the git client or the egress gateway.
- **Dispatch**: spawn packs the archives, calls create, and returns the session id once the first run has started (`worker-api.md:17`). A failed workspace setup leaves the session failed and returns the error.
- **Steer**: a prompt maps to a follow-up or a steer (`session.ts:264-282`). While a question waits, any prompt becomes a steer and is queued until the answer.
- **Question**: `ask_parent` stores the question and moves the session to waiting. The state goes over the socket to the helper `watch`, which wakes the parent with the session, question id and text. The parent calls the answer tool (`question-round-trip.md:38-48`).
- **Collect**: finish and failure wakes carry the last message or the failure (`plugin.md:83-89`). The messages tool returns the last N root-conversation entries. On pi, `tentacles_wait` blocks. Claude Code has no wait tool, because helper processes are capped at ten minutes (`plugin.md:78-79`).
- **Local list**: the plugin keeps a local session list, a pi session entry or a `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` file, and syncs it from the Worker at harness start (`plugin.md:101-136`).

**4. Trade-offs the docs name**
- There is no explicit comparison with pi-coding-agent, and the repo has no mention of it. The docs name these differences from a local agent:
  - Nothing runs locally. Parent-side state and output are reachable only through the tools (`plugin.md:62`).
  - Skills, agents and context are fixed at spawn. Context edits stay remote and never come back (`product-design/remote-agents.md:21-23`).
  - The isolate shell has no node or npm and returns output only when the command ends. The container has a cold start of about 1 to 3 seconds (`computer-workspace.md:21,30,92`).
  - A container stop loses running processes and anything outside `/workspace`, including mise runtimes (`computer-workspace.md:35`).
  - `npm install` was slower in the synced workspace: 11.4 s against 4.8 s on the container's disk (`computer-workspace.md:40`).
  - A headless `claude -p` parent never gets wakes (`plugin.md:98-99`).
  - Deleted sessions linger in the local list until the plugin learns of them (`plugin.md:141`).
  - Unpushed work is lost with the session a month after its last run (`remote-agents.md:66`).
  - Containers can be placed outside North America, and nothing enforces the region (`deploy.md:90-91`).
  - Cloudflare hosts every role in a single deploy. Mixing providers was considered and not taken (`runtime-components.md:112-113`).

I did not read `core/src/session/state.ts` or the plugin helper client in depth. The wire format of each call is in `packages/worker-api/src/sessions.ts`, which I did not open. The version of pi-durable is pinned at 1.5.1 (`pnpm-workspace.yaml:31`).
